terms.comment: Of music itself: īnstrūmentum mūsicum, lēgēs mūsicae, the rules of music. As a noun a musician (Cic. Off. 1.146); in Terence also of poetry (Lewis & Short). Of a person who loves music, Latin uses a phrase, as Pliny calls the dolphin mūsicae artī amīcum.

terms.gloss: tuneful, melodious (of a voice or a sound)
evidence: Cic. Brut. 234: vōce suāvī et canōrā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a voice or an instrument that sings well; of a speaker’s voice it can also be a fault, a sing-song (Cic. Off. 1.133, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: delphīnus nōn hominī tantum amīcum animal, vērum et mūsicae artī
phrases.english: the dolphin, an animal friendly not only to man but also to music

sources: Lewis & Short: musicus · Lewis & Short: canorus
